summary: The newsletter half of this domain survives adversarial review essentially intact: three crons are registered in vercel.json (newsletter-send */2, newsletter-reconcile hourly, newsletter-monthly-draft daily), the draft cron self-heals on a Pacific 1st-of-month check and drafts-only, the admin surface is nav-reachable (lib/admin/nav.ts:187), and the Resend webhook is genuinely fail-closed on a missing secret. The "send layer" half does not survive. The prior auditor was too generous on three counts. First, it claimed the newsletter send path is "fully instrumented end to end (attribution + recordEmailEvent 'sent')" — lib/newsletter/send-queue.ts calls attributeOutbound but never calls recordEmailEvent at all; newsletters keep their own separate ledger and are absent from email_events 'sent'. Second, and far more serious than anything in the original report: lib/cma/send.ts:352 and lib/bpo/send.ts:383 send via GMAIL as the primary transport with Resend only as a failure fallback, so the Resend webhook is structurally blind to every SUCCESSFUL CMA and BPO send — not just missing a 'sent' row, but missing delivered, bounced, and complained, which also means the webhook's bounce-driven addSuppression never fires for those recipients. Third, the auditor asserted no self-serve preference center exists; one does (app/account/notifications/page.tsx + DashboardNotificationPrefs), and it is worse than absent because only app/actions/saved-search-alerts.ts:203-210 reads notification_preferences — the newsletter, market-report, CMA, and BPO paths ignore it silently. Net: "ONE send layer" is missing, not partial, and the "unified engagement store" is partial, not have.

items.requirement: Newsletter auto-generates and Matt can see who's getting it / who's opening it
items.evidence: CONFIRMED. app/api/cron/newsletter-monthly-draft/route.ts:69-101 — requireCronAuth, dayOfMonthPacific()!==1 no-op, findNewsletterIdBySubject idempotency, produceNewsletterDraft('cron:newsletter-monthly-draft'), notifyMatt() sending both a Resend email and queueBrokerHealthAlert SMS. All three crons ARE in vercel.json (lines 4, 8, 12). app/api/cron/newsletter-send/route.ts:20-33 calls enqueueDueScheduled()+drainAllSending(); lib/newsletter/send-queue.ts:431 finalizeRecipient(c.id,'sent'|'failed'). lib/data/newsletter/queue.ts:47 flips the issue to status='sending' with a lock_token on approve, :359-373 resets stale claims. Admin pages exist at app/admin/(protected)/newsletters/{page,new/page,[id]/page,subscribers/page,analytics/page}.tsx and the analytics page imports getBrokerNewsletterAnalytics from '@/lib/data' (line 7). REACHABILITY VERIFIED beyond the original audit: lib/admin/nav.ts:187 registers { label: 'Newsletters', href: '/admin/newsletters', capability: 'content.marketing' } — the auditor never checked this and it is the single most common way a feature like this turns out to be dead.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Mechanics are real and reachable. Adding one gap the auditor did not name: lib/newsletter/send-queue.ts writes NO row to email_events, so the newsletter is invisible to lib/data/crm/getContactEmailEngagement.ts (which reads only email_events at line 103). Matt's contact-record engagement tile therefore does not count newsletter sends. Per-issue newsletter stats work because they read the separate newsletter_recipient_events ledger. Still not verified: whether a real issue has reached status='sent' in production.
items.why_it_matters: This is the one genuinely finished pipeline in the domain; it should be the template the other send paths are refactored toward.

items.requirement: Open/click tracking for the newsletter, with ESP webhook registered
items.evidence: CONFIRMED, evidence checked line by line. app/api/webhooks/resend/route.ts:41-51 rejects with a 500 when RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (fail closed in ALL envs, dev-allow branch explicitly removed), :52-61 verifySvixSignature + isFreshTimestamp, 401 on failure. app/api/track/e/open/route.ts:65-71 recordEmailEvent + :77-84 recordNewsletterEngagement; app/api/track/e/click/route.ts:47 same pair. lib/newsletter/track-ledger.ts:38-58 parses 'newsletter:<id>', resolves the recipient via getRecipientForPerson, writes recordLedgerEvent with a recipient-scoped dedupe key. Both email_events (docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT.md:2233) and newsletter_recipient_events (:2987) exist in the snapshot.
items.gap: [VERIFIED] Correct as reported. Reinforcing the auditor's own caveat with a stronger reason to trust it: the webhook ALSO drives suppression on hard bounce/complaint (route.ts:177-193 addSuppression), so if it were not actually registered in the Resend dashboard, bounce suppression would be silently dead everywhere. That is a load-bearing dependency on an out-of-repo config that nothing in CI checks.
items.why_it_matters: An unregistered webhook would silently disable bounce/complaint suppression brand-wide, which is a sender-reputation and CAN-SPAM exposure, not just a reporting gap.

items.requirement: ONE outbound send layer that all send types (newsletter, CMA, BPO, market report, saved search, CRM one-off, CRM SMS, sequences) route through
items.evidence: [Downgraded from the auditor's 'partial'.] There is no send layer — only three optional helpers that callers may or may not invoke. lib/resend.ts sendEmail() is a bare wrapper with zero auto-instrumentation. Grep for recordEmailEvent across lib+app returns exactly FIVE non-test call sites: lib/crm/market-report-send.ts:185, app/actions/saved-search-alerts.ts:352, app/api/cma-drafts/[id]/send/route.ts:138, app/api/track/e/{open:65,click:47}, app/api/webhooks/resend/route.ts:148. Everything else is uninstrumented. CORRECTIONS TO THE AUDITOR: (a) it claimed the newsletter is fully instrumented — lib/newsletter/send-queue.ts imports attributeOutbound (line 7) and sendEmail (line 6) and calls NEITHER recordEmailEvent nor anything writing email_events; (b) it claimed lib/cma-deliver.ts is a distinct path but never checked it — the ACTIVE finalize-deliver path (app/api/cma/[slug]/finalize-deliver/route.ts:36) uses instrumentEmailHtml (lib/cma-deliver.ts:29,318), NOT attributeOutbound, and has no recordEmailEvent; (c) THE BIG MISS — lib/cma/send.ts:352 and lib/bpo/send.ts:383 both set transport='gmail' and use sendEmail (Resend) ONLY as a fallback when Gmail fails, so on the happy path these emails never touch Resend and the webhook cannot emit delivered/opened/clicked/bounced/complained for them at all. lib/cma-delivery.ts (legacy, still reachable via app/api/cma-delivery/route.ts:22) has no tracking, no recordEmailEvent, and no suppression check — though it emails the assigned broker for review (lib/cma-delivery.ts:372-392), not a lead, which limits the compliance exposure.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor rated this 'partial' and named the newsletter as one of four fully-instrumented paths — it is not instrumented into email_events at all. It also missed that CMA and BPO send over Gmail, so those recipients are invisible to the Resend webhook entirely, meaning no delivered, no bounce, no complaint, and therefore no bounce-driven suppression — a strictly worse failure than the 'missing sent event' it described.] Nine independent compose+send implementations, each opting in to tracking and measurement by hand: lib/newsletter/send-queue.ts, lib/crm/market-report-send.ts, app/actions/saved-search-alerts.ts, lib/crm/bulk-handlers/email-cohort.ts, lib/cma/send.ts, lib/cma-deliver.ts, lib/cma-delivery.ts, app/actions/contact-cma.ts, app/api/cma-drafts/[id]/send/route.ts, lib/bpo/send.ts, lib/cma/request-emails.ts. No chokepoint, no gate, nothing preventing the next one from skipping everything.
items.why_it_matters: The stated promise — everything a contact received and everything they clicked — cannot be delivered from a store that most send paths never write to, on a transport the webhook cannot observe.

items.requirement: Bulk send capability: bulk send out searches, market reports, or whatever, or send them out individually
items.evidence: Bulk engine confirmed real and reachable: app/api/cron/crm-bulk-worker is in vercel.json:20; lib/crm/bulk-handlers/index.ts:44-60 registers 14 handlers plus registerEmailCohortHandler() at :65; EMAIL_COHORT_KIND='email-cohort' (lib/crm/bulk-handlers/email-cohort.ts:55) is in the BulkKind union (lib/crm/bulk-helpers.ts:49); UI path components/admin/crm/bulk/registry.tsx:253 jobKind:'email-cohort' -> app/actions/crm-bulk.ts:347 enqueue(). Idempotent per-recipient claim via insertEmailEvent (email-cohort.ts:227-237) — this handler DOES write email_events. TWO THINGS THE AUDITOR MISSED: (1) app/admin/(protected)/newsletters/BulkOneOffForm.tsx is exactly the 'blast this specific already-built deliverable to a cohort now' action it declared not built — it sends THIS draft issue to a pasted email list OR a CRM tag, through adminBulkOneOffSendAction and the same suppression-checked drain; (2) app/api/cron/crm-scheduled-sends/route.ts:83 is registered in vercel.json:24 and enqueues 'email-cohort' jobs on a schedule, a whole scheduling tier the audit did not mention.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: a one-time cohort blast of a specific built deliverable DOES exist for the newsletter (BulkOneOffForm.tsx), and a scheduled-send cron exists (crm-scheduled-sends, vercel.json:24) — both were omitted.] The real remaining gaps are narrower than reported: (a) no SMS bulk handler — the BulkKind union (lib/crm/bulk-helpers.ts:40-49) has zero SMS kinds and grep for sendSms across lib/crm/bulk-handlers/ returns nothing; (b) the one-time blast exists only for a newsletter ISSUE — there is still no equivalent for a specific market report or a specific saved-search result set; crm:set-report-subscription and crm:assign-saved-search create ongoing subscriptions only.
items.why_it_matters: Two of the four things Matt asked for are already built and were about to be re-built; the two that are genuinely missing (SMS bulk, one-time market-report blast) are much smaller scopes than the original report implied.

items.requirement: Unified engagement store recording delivered/opened/clicked across all send types
items.evidence: [Downgraded from the auditor's 'have'.] email_events is real and singular (docs/DATABASE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT.md:2233), read by lib/data/crm/getContactEmailEngagement.ts:103 and rendered at app/admin/(protected)/crm/[id]/page.tsx:168,665 via components/admin/crm/ContactEmailEngagement.tsx — that chain is verified reachable. But it is NOT unified across send types. Writers are only: the Resend webhook (app/api/webhooks/resend/route.ts:148, always sendType:'other' — content-type breakdown lost), the two first-party tracking routes, market-report-send, saved-search-alerts, cma-drafts/[id]/send, and email-cohort. Not written by: the newsletter send path, lib/cma/send.ts, lib/bpo/send.ts, lib/cma-deliver.ts, lib/cma-delivery.ts, app/actions/contact-cma.ts. And because CMA/BPO go out over Gmail (lib/cma/send.ts:352, lib/bpo/send.ts:383), the webhook cannot backfill them either. Per-artifact join absent as reported: lib/data/crm/getContactCmas.ts:36 reads only .from('cmas'), getContactBpos.ts:36 only .from('broker_price_opinions'), neither touches email_events.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: rated 'have'; it is partial at best. The auditor's framing — 'BPO/most-CMA sends get open/click tracked but never get a sent event' — understates it. On the Gmail happy path those sends produce no delivered, no bounce, and no complaint either, so the aggregate tile undercounts every dimension for CMA/BPO, and the newsletter contributes nothing to it at all.] Two layered gaps: (1) coverage — the store is missing entire send types, not just one event kind; (2) granularity — no per-item join, so no CMA or BPO row can display 'opened on 7/18'.
items.why_it_matters: A contact-record engagement tile that silently omits newsletters, CMAs, and BPOs will be read by Matt as truth and is not.

items.evidence: [Status unchanged but the finding is materially different from the auditor's.] A self-serve preference center DOES exist and IS live: app/account/notifications/page.tsx renders components/dashboard/DashboardNotificationPrefs backed by profiles.notification_preferences (app/actions/profile.ts:41,58,81). The auditor stated no such surface exists. The problem is that almost nothing reads it: grep for notification_preferences across lib+app returns exactly ONE consuming send path, app/actions/saved-search-alerts.ts:203-210 (emailEnabled). The newsletter, market-report, CMA, and BPO send paths never read it. Global unsubscribe machinery is real and correct: lib/data/newsletter/index.ts:126-178 writes a global crm_suppressions row; app/api/email/unsubscribe/route.ts implements RFC 8058 properly — GET renders a confirm page only (explicitly refusing to suppress on a mail-client prefetch, lines 10-13) and POST calls addSuppression through the chokepoint.
items.gap: [CORRECTED: the auditor said 'there is no granular self-serve preference center' — there is one, at /account/notifications, and it has been live. The real defect is worse than absence: a user who unticks email notifications there will still receive newsletters, market reports, CMAs, and BPOs, because only saved-search alerts honor the setting. A preference control that silently does nothing for four of five channels is a consent-representation problem, not merely a missing feature.] Separately, newsletter unsubscribe remains an all-marketing-email opt-out by design (lib/data/newsletter/index.ts:139-146), which is a defensible CAN-SPAM posture but is not the per-type dial the UI implies.
items.why_it_matters: Showing a user a preference toggle that four of five send paths ignore misrepresents consent and is the kind of thing that turns into a complaint rather than a bug report.

items.requirement: Compliance: CAN-SPAM footer, TCPA STOP handling, litigator/DNC hard-stop tags
items.evidence: CONFIRMED against source. lib/email/prepare.ts builds the multipart body, visible unsubscribe link, postal address, and RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe headers. app/api/twilio/inbound-sms/route.ts:27-165 STOP/START keyword handling calling addSuppression(channel:'sms', reason:'stop-keyword'). lib/crm/suppressions.ts TAG_CHANNEL:19-27 maps compliance:hard-stop to all channels and contact:do-not-call to call+sms. lib/crm/bulk-helpers.ts PROTECTED_TAG_LITERALS/PREFIXES is derived from the SAME TAG_CHANNEL array so a bulk tag op can never strip a compliance tag — verified, and stronger than the auditor described. Suppression gating IS more consistent than measurement: lib/cma/send.ts:307-308, lib/bpo/send.ts:299, lib/cma-deliver.ts:293-294 all check isSuppressed/isSuppressedByEmail before sending.
items.gap: [VERIFIED with two additions the auditor missed.] (1) lib/cma-delivery.ts (legacy, reachable via app/api/cma-delivery/route.ts) has NO suppression check anywhere — grep for isSuppressed returns nothing. Exposure is limited because its send at :383 targets assignedBroker.email (an internal review notification), not a lead, so this is a latent hazard rather than a live violation, but it should be deleted rather than left reachable. (2) The Gmail-primary transport on CMA/BPO means the Resend webhook's bounce/complaint -> addSuppression path (webhooks/resend/route.ts:177-193) never fires for those recipients, so a CMA sent to a dead address will keep being sent to.
items.why_it_matters: Compliance gating is the one layer in this domain that is genuinely mature; the two holes are containable and worth closing before they become live.

shared_primitives_needed: One canonical sendTrackedEmail() that folds isSuppressed + prepareDeliverableEmail + attributeOutbound + recordEmailEvent('sent') into a single call, with lib/resend.ts sendEmail() made private to it, plus a mechanical gate (the CLAUDE.md G50 canonical-composer pattern) that fails the commit on any new direct sendEmail import outside the wrapper. Prose will not hold this line — nine paths already drifted.

A transport-agnostic measurement contract: because CMA and BPO send over Gmail, not Resend, the wrapper must record 'sent' itself rather than relying on the Resend webhook, and Gmail-rail sends need an equivalent bounce signal (Gmail API delivery-failure polling or a bounce-mailbox watch) or those recipients will never be suppressed on bounce.

A per-artifact engagement join: extend getContactCmas / getContactBpos / newsletter readers to look up email_events by emailKey (e.g. 'cma:<slug>') so each list row shows its own sent/opened/clicked timestamp instead of only an aggregate tile.

Make profiles.notification_preferences an actual input to the suppression chokepoint so the /account/notifications toggles bind on every send path, not only saved-search alerts — or remove the toggles that do nothing.

Delete lib/cma-delivery.ts and its route, and pick ONE canonical CMA send among lib/cma/send.ts, lib/cma-deliver.ts, app/actions/contact-cma.ts, app/api/cma-drafts/[id]/send/route.ts, routing the rest through it.
An SMS bulk handler registered in lib/crm/bulk-handlers/index.ts, if bulk SMS parity is actually wanted.

Generalize the existing BulkOneOffForm pattern (blast THIS built artifact to a cohort) from newsletters to market reports and saved-search result sets — the mechanism already exists and only needs a second and third artifact type.
open_questions_for_owner: The /account/notifications preference toggles are live but only saved-search alerts honor them — a contact who turns off email there still gets newsletters, market reports, CMAs, and BPOs. Do you want those toggles wired into the suppression chokepoint so they bind everywhere, or removed until they do? Leaving them as-is misrepresents consent.

CMA and BPO email sends go out over Gmail from the broker's mailbox, with Resend only as a failure fallback. That is almost certainly the right deliverability choice for a personal broker-to-client document, but it means Resend's bounce and complaint handling never sees those sends. Do you want to keep Gmail-primary and build a separate bounce signal for that rail, or move CMA/BPO to Resend for observability?

Bulk one-time blast: BulkOneOffForm already does exactly this for a newsletter issue (pasted list or CRM tag). Do you want the same control generalized to market reports and saved-search results, or is subscription-based recurring delivery sufficient for those?

Should newsletter unsubscribe stay an all-marketing-email opt-out (current, CAN-SPAM-conservative), or become a per-content-type dial? This is the same decision as the preferences question above and should be answered once.
Has a real monthly issue completed draft to approved to 'sent' in production? The code path is verified complete and reachable, but nothing in the repo proves it has been exercised end to end.
